newsitem.title: USA: Rosie O'Donnell to host expanded Tony awards show.
newsitem.headline: Rosie O'Donnell to host expanded Tony awards show.

text.p: If you want hot comic and daytime talk show star Rosie O'Donnell to host your awards programme, all you have to do is promise her a platform fit for a star.

O'Donnell said Wednesday that she will host the 1997 Tony Awards on June 1 because the producers gave her the biggest theatre in New York -- the 6,000-seat Radio City Music Hall -- as the place to hand out Broadway's version of the Oscars.
Location, location, location -- as they say in New York real estate circles.

"I didn't say do it my way or else. I said I would be happy to do it if it was moved to a bigger place and I would be happy to use my millions of viewers to promote it," O'Donnell, who has an audience of 6 million for her daytime talk show, told a news conference.

Securing O'Donnell and Radio City, an Art Deco show palace that is one of the architectural masterworks of New York, are just two moves made by the producers to boost the audience for the usually low-rated annual Broadway honours show.

The've also added an extra hour to the programme and an extra network to show it. The first hour, which will be shown on the Public Broadcasting System (PBS), will be devoted to presenting awards for craftsman categories such as best direction of a play or musical to best lighting, scenery, choreography and orchestration.

The next two hours, which will include all the major awards, will be shown on CBS, which has aired the programme for 20 years. The changes give the network more time to show musical production numbers, scenes from plays and acceptance speeches from winners.
CBS was criticised last year for limiting acceptance speeches to almost the blink of an eye.
